clue.text: Ban for hospital — one was effective

parts.note: pro is Latin for 'for', as in pros and cons
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital
the Roman numeral for one is I
a brake or a measure that bit took hold and worked

explanation.surface: A hospital rule was banned once it had done its job.
explanation.definitionFit: To prohibit something is to forbid it, a verb synonym of ban.

clue.text: Hold back reserve coach

parts.note: to coach someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A sports coach keeps a reserve player on the bench.
explanation.definitionFit: To restrain is to curb or check, so it means hold back.

clue.text: Bird runs round yard ahead of a carnivore

indicators.note: the enclosed piece comes in front of the letter A in the answer
the bird's letters run round the outside of the yard abbreviation, enclosing it

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: A bird dashes round the farmyard, keeping clear of a predator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runs round' puts HEN around Y to give HYEN, and 'ahead of' sets that before A.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyena is a meat-eating African mammal, so an example of a carnivore.

clue.text: Ma in beach thing, maybe, which the Victorians used?

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged some other way, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: Mother sits inside some seaside contraption from Victorian days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges the fourteen letters of MA IN BEACH THING. A bathing machine was a wheeled hut rolled into the sea so Victorian bathers could change and enter the water unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: Victorian seaside visitors used these wheeled changing huts for modest sea bathing, so the description fits by example.

clue.text: It's the right time to get over that

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declares this is the right moment to get past some problem.
explanation.definitionFit: Thereon means upon that matter, a formal equivalent of over that.

clue.text: Man gets post, we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals that the word is judged by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: post delivered to the door is mail

explanation.surface: A man receives his letters in the morning delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: A male is a man or boy, a person of the masculine sex.

clue.text: One catching fish in the sea finds answer in amalgamation

definitions.text: One catching fish in the sea

indicators.note: in places the answer abbreviation inside the word for an amalgamation

parts.note: a merger is an amalgamation of firms

explanation.surface: A trawler crew finds the solution lies in combining forces at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The merganser is a diving duck with a serrated bill for gripping fish, so the long definition describes it rather than naming it.
explanation.definitionFit: The merganser is a fish-eating sea duck, so it is a bird that catches fish.

clue.text: Boy taking Oxford course is overtaken by a faster mover

indicators.note: taking means the word for boy takes in the course abbreviation, holding it inside

parts.note: a lad is a boy
PPE, Philosophy, Politics and Economics, is a famous Oxford degree course

explanation.surface: A student reading PPE at Oxford gets outrun by a quicker athlete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a racecourse, fitting the lapping picture, but it is the university degree.
explanation.definitionFit: In a race, a runner who is lapped has been overtaken by a rival a full circuit ahead.

clue.text: Study fellow in Earls Court with new design for aileron?

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn

indicators.note: a new design means the letters are laid out in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A scholar in a London district works on a fresh design for an aircraft part.
explanation.walkthrough: Earls Court is a district of west London. The question mark shows aileron is one example of the answer, not a synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: An aileron is a hinged flap on a wing that steers the aircraft, a type of control surface.

clue.text: Agreement in the manner dispatched

parts.note: as means in the manner of, as in 'do as I do'
something dispatched has been sent

explanation.surface: Approval granted in the way a letter is posted.
explanation.definitionFit: Assent is formal approval or consent, a synonym of agreement.

clue.text: I journey — a vain experience

parts.note: the ego is the self, the 'I'
a trip is a journey

explanation.surface: Someone describes their travels as an exercise in vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego-trip is an activity pursued to boost self-importance, so a vain experience.

clue.text: Credit to dine I have found original

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
to eat is to dine
I've is the contraction of I have

explanation.surface: A diner praises the inventive cooking they have discovered.
explanation.definitionFit: Creative work shows imagination and novelty, which is what original means here.

clue.text: Old foreign coin showing the king — about a pound

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go round the others, enclosing them

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for the pound, from Latin libra
R stands for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: An antique coin bearing the monarch's head is worth roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AL inside THER, making TH-AL-ER.
explanation.definitionFit: The thaler was a large silver coin of the German states, the source of the word dollar.

clue.text: Fraudulent, bogus nun with disguise concealing nothing

indicators.note: concealing means the disguise letters hold the nothing letter within them
bogus means fake, signalling the letters are not in their real order

parts.note: O, the round figure zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A fake nun in a disguise hides something underhand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bogus' rearranges NUN and DISGUISE into DISINGENUS, and 'concealing' sets O inside that, before the final U-S.
explanation.definitionFit: Disingenuous behaviour is insincere and deceptive, close in sense to fraudulent.

clue.text: Job description follows fashionable person found in ward

indicators.note: follows means the description comes after the fashionable word

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
the biblical Job is proverbially patient, 'the patience of Job'

explanation.surface: An employment brief comes after a trendy candidate turns up at the office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Job' at the start of the clue hides its capital: it is the Old Testament figure famous for patience, not employment.
explanation.definitionFit: An in-patient stays on a hospital ward overnight or longer.

clue.text: Looking over second old PM

parts.note: George Canning was British Prime Minister in 1827

explanation.surface: A former prime minister glances at something a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: Scanning a page means looking it over quickly.

clue.text: To do best I'd back rigorous identification of beauty spot

parts.note: to peak is to reach one's highest point

indicators.note: back means the contraction I'd is read in reverse

parts.note: strict means rigorous

explanation.surface: A determined walker aims to pin down exactly which famous viewpoint to visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ID into DI. The Peak District is a national park of hills and moorland in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The Peak District is a celebrated area of scenery in England, so a beauty spot.

clue.text: Stupid person put mat on a road

parts.note: mat, a variant of matt, describes a dull unpolished finish

explanation.surface: Someone foolishly lays a doormat in the middle of the street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mat' is the adjective (matt), not the floor covering.
explanation.definitionFit: A dullard is a slow-witted person, a dunce.

clue.text: Joseph keeps function merry

indicators.note: keeps means the name holds the function inside it

parts.note: Joe is the short form of Joseph
cos, cosine, is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: Joseph holds on to his role at a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'function' sounds like a party, matching 'merry', but it is the mathematical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocose means playful and humorous, near in sense to merry.

clue.text: Drink? Feverish child imbibes nothing

indicators.note: imbibes means taking something in, so the letters swallow the nothing letter

parts.note: a feverish person feels hot
O, shaped like zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A sick child with a temperature refuses anything to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibes' puts O inside HOTCH. Hootch is slang for alcoholic liquor, especially cheap spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Hootch is informal for strong liquor, a kind of alcoholic beverage.

clue.text: Petty aristocrat, old girl

clue.text: Solid changes to bathing places

indicators.note: changes says the letters of the first word alter their order

explanation.surface: Something firm turns into swimming pools.
explanation.definitionFit: A lido is a public open-air swimming pool, a place for bathing.

clue.text: One in a canoe getting round large part of world

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the rearranged letters
getting round suggests turning about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A paddler in a canoe circles a big stretch of the globe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting round' rearranges A CANOE to OCEANA, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Oceania is the region covering Australia, New Zealand and the Pacific islands, a vast area of the globe.

clue.text: Insecticide finds its way into animal drink

indicators.note: finds its way into says the answer is tucked inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pesticide gets into an animal's water supply.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldrin is an organochlorine chemical once widely used to kill insects.

clue.text: Cats needing tails put back — it's a nuisance

indicators.note: tails put back says the final letters of the word are turned round

parts.note: cats are kept as pets

explanation.surface: Cats whose tails must be tucked away are a bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tails put back' swaps the last two letters of PETS.
explanation.definitionFit: A pest is an annoying person or thing, a nuisance.

clue.text: Competition to get English ship into improved grade

indicators.note: into means the English ship goes inside the rearranged grade
improved means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: SS, steamship, prefixes ship names

explanation.surface: A competitor must move an English vessel into a higher class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improved' rearranges GRADE to DRAGE, and 'into' places ESS within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is a competitive equestrian event judged on precise horse movements.
